steps.title: Factors: study variable groups
steps.text: In mzTab-M 2.1, study_variable_group[n] describes one experimental factor. This file has two: sex, a categorical variable with text values, and timepoint, an ordinal variable with integer values in days. study_variable_refs lists the study variables that are the levels of the factor. type and datatype take a STATO term and an XML Schema type, so that tools know how to compare the levels.

steps.title: Levels: study variables
steps.text: Each study_variable[n] is one level of one factor: Female and Male for sex, 0, 1 and 2 for timepoint. assay_refs lists the assays that carry the level, so every assay appears once under each factor. In the summary, abundance_study_variable[n] gives the abundance of a molecule for each level.

steps.title: Design cells: assays
steps.text: An assay is one cell of the design, a combination of one level of each factor, such as Female_0day. ms_run_ref names the run that measured it. Read backwards through assay_refs, assay[2] belongs to Female (study_variable[1]) and to 1 day (study_variable[4]).

steps.title: The 2 x 3 design
steps.text: The comments at the top of the file draw the design: two sexes times three timepoints give six assays, one per cell. The summary row reports D-gluconic acid in each of the six assays and in each of the five study variables, two for sex and three for timepoint. abundance_study_variable[1] (Female, 1.52) is the mean of the three female assays (1.51, 1.62 and 1.44).

steps.title: Describe your own design
steps.text: To describe your own design, give each factor a study_variable_group, each level a study_variable with its assays, and validate the file on the 2.1 engine. study_variable_group is new in mzTab-M 2.1: a 2.0 file describes factors with study_variable[n]-factors, which the 2.1 engine reports (Warn-2067). This file has only a summary section and declares the profile M+S.
